title: Open the AlpineFit case
casePrompt: AlpineFit, a regional fitness-club chain, grew membership but saw operating margin fall from 18% to 12% last year. The CEO wants to understand why and what to do next.

responseCycle.prompt: Restate the decision objective in your own words before asking questions.
guidance: Name the metric, direction of change, and decision to support.

criteria.label: Names operating margin and its decline
Connects the diagnosis to what AlpineFit should do

comparison.title: One strong opening
comparison.text: I want to identify what drove AlpineFit's six-point margin decline last year and determine the most practical actions to restore profitability without undermining membership growth.

questionOptions.label: How is operating margin defined, and is the decline chain-wide?
questionOptions.response: Operating margin is operating profit divided by revenue, and the decline appears across the chain rather than in one isolated club.

questionOptions.label: Did the decline occur gradually or at a particular point last year?
questionOptions.response: Most of the decline developed over the last nine months and persisted through year-end.

questionOptions.label: Are there constraints on pricing, investment, or member experience?
questionOptions.response: The CEO will consider operational investment but does not want a broad price increase or service cuts that could damage retention.

questionOptions.label: Has AlpineFit changed its logo or brand colors recently?
questionOptions.response: No. Branding has not changed and is not believed to affect the margin decline.

questionOptions.label: Can we interview every club manager before forming a structure?
questionOptions.response: That would take several weeks; the CEO expects an initial fact-based direction much sooner.
